title: "Quickstart"

## Install

The command-line tool:

```bash
uv tool install questionsafe        # or: pipx install questionsafe
```

As a library in a Python project:

```bash
uv add questionsafe                 # or: pip install questionsafe
```

The release on PyPI lags behind the repository. For the current version, install from
GitHub, e.g. `uv tool install git+https://github.com/kenjisato/questionsafe`.

## Two ways to write questions

**Markdown files** suit most question banks: one question per file, YAML front matter for
the settings, the body for the question text.

```markdown
---
type: singlechoice
name: Japan/Capital
---

What is the capital of Japan?

## /choices

- (x) Tokyo
- ( ) Osaka
- ( ) Kyoto
```

```bash
questionsafe validate capital.md
questionsafe render capital.md --out capital.xml   # import this into Moodle
```

Next: [Markdown Schema](markdown.qmd) for every key, [Command Line](commandline.md) for
projects and templates.

**Python** suits generated questions and variants:

```python
from questionsafe import Q, Quiz

q = (
    Q.SingleChoice("Japan/Capital")
    .ask("What is the capital of Japan?")
    .set_choice_correct("Tokyo")
    .set_choices_wrong("Osaka", "Kyoto")
)
Quiz([q]).to_xml("capital.xml")
```

Next: [Python API](python.qmd), and [MetaChoice](metachoice.qmd) for generating variants
from a pool of choices.

The two mix: `Reader("capital.md").read()` turns a Markdown file into a question object,
which can go into a `Quiz` with questions built in Python.
